proposal.root_cause: Billing import rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, E-13) compares raw register values to 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling='none'; v4.2-firmware meters report in 0.1 m3 units vs legacy v3.x whole m3 (E-14), so BV-17 misflags normal v4.2 consumption as abnormally high, causing 95.5% (1,184/1,240) of the ESTIMATED-cohort disputed bills to be rejected as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION and estimate-substituted (E-12). This explains only the ESTIMATED cohort; the mechanism for the larger ACTUAL-read cohort (1,785/3,025, E-01) remains unresolved (U-ACTUAL-COHORT-MECHANISM, OPEN, CRITICAL).

remedies.description: Correct BV-17 to apply a firmware-aware unit-scaling factor (0.1 m3 for v4.2 vs m3 for v3.x) before the high-consumption comparison, i.e. escalate_billing_rule_fix to SH-BILL/billing-config as already scoped in PD-1 and SC-BV17-REJECTION-RATE-NORMALIZ.
remedies.feasibility_rationale: The escalation/config-change action is within PD-1's intended_scope and no active constraint (K-BILLWRITE, K-DISPATCH) blocks a validation-rule correction; it is a read/config-review path, achievable within the 181-minute remaining budget.
remedies.residual_gap: Does not address whether already-rejected v4.2 reads need retroactive reprocessing (U-BV17-FIX-RETROACTIVE, OPEN) and leaves the larger ACTUAL-read cohort's mechanism (1,785/3,025) completely unaddressed.

proposal.summary: Customer Service (SH-CS) requested an AI agent to auto-answer billing dispute tickets and auto-fix wrong bills (CL-01), framing the issue as a response-speed problem. Investigation found response times are within SLA (E-02), so the real problem was redefined (PD-1, superseding invalidated PD-1@v1) as: billing import rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 (E-13), compares raw meter register values to 12-month history without unit scaling; this misreads v4.2-firmware meters' "0.1 m3" units (vs legacy v3.x whole m3, E-14) as abnormally high consumption, wrongly rejecting valid reads (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) and forcing estimate substitution. This explains 95.5% (1,184/1,240) of the disputed ESTIMATED-read-type bills (E-12, corroborated by E-15/E-16/E-17), coinciding with the dispute-ticket surge from ~600/month to ~1,180-1,260/month starting August (E-07). Alternative causes were ruled out: tariff change (E-03/E-05), ticket-handling delay (E-02), AMI/MDMS read failure (E-12/E-16/E-17 contradict H-AMI-MDMS-READ-FAILURE), and field-staffing shortage (E-12/E-17 contradict H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE, despite SH-FIELD's claim CL-03/E-06 which carries an incentive bias and was invalidated as a reliable explanation). The release scope (SD-2) covers querying the rule-change log, analyzing disputed bills by read type, and escalating the BV-17 fix to SH-BILL (escalate_billing_rule_fix) — a prevention-only structural correction, not automated bill writes (no automated write_bill_adjustment occurs, per K-BILLWRITE and SC-NO-UNAUTHORIZED-BILL-WRITES). The decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION: the diagnosed and escalatable BV-17 fix is delivered now, while several unresolved items are explicitly deferred rather than blocking release.
key_points: Root problem established: billing import rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, E-13) compares raw register values without unit scaling, misreading v4.2-firmware meters' 0.1 m3 units as abnormally high (vs v3.x whole m3, E-14), causing wrongful REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION rejections.

This mechanism explains 95.5% (1,184/1,240) of disputed ESTIMATED-read-cohort bills (E-12), cross-confirmed by billing-db and mdms-export (E-15, E-16, E-17), coinciding with the dispute surge starting August 2026 (E-07).

Alternative hypotheses were tested and rejected with evidence: tariff change (E-03), slow ticket response (E-02, within SLA), AMI/MDMS read failure (E-12/E-16/E-17), and field-staffing shortage (E-12/E-17 contradict SH-FIELD's claim E-06/CL-03, which carries a stated headcount-increase incentive).

The original request (CL-01, SH-CS) to build an auto-fix/auto-answer AI agent was a stakeholder framing, not the established problem; the actual fix is a billing-config rule correction escalated to SH-BILL, with no automated bill writes performed, consistent with K-BILLWRITE authority constraint.

Release scope (SD-2) includes querying the rule-change log (DA-RULES), analyzing disputed bills by read type (DA-TICKET), and escalating the BV-17 fix to SH-BILL; this is prevention-focused, not retroactive correction.

Decision: RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, following a DEFINE Gate CONDITIONAL_PASS, with several verification obligations (VOBs) deferred as open and explicitly out of release scope rather than resolved.
limitations_explained: The larger ACTUAL-read-type disputed-bill cohort (1,785 of 3,025) has an unestablished error mechanism; the BV-17 fix only addresses the ESTIMATED-read cohort, and this diagnostic work (VOB-U-ACTUAL-COHORT-MECHANISM, OPEN, CRITICAL) is excluded from this release.

Monthly dispute-ticket volume (M-DISPUTE-VOLUME) is not a reliable proof that bills are actually correct, since ticket-handling or response-template changes could suppress ticket creation without fixing billing errors (VOB-U-METRIC-VALIDITY-TICKET-VOLUM, OPEN, HIGH); ticket-volume monitoring is excluded from this release.
